title: Beginner, 15 gold trading ideas, all rejected by my own pre-written criteria. Please tear apart my method.
author: Powerful-Feed4318
selftext:
I'm a beginner in programming and finance. For about a month I have been running a small personal research lab ("Nucleus") on gold (XAUUSD CFD) with MT5 EAs and Python screening. **No real money, ever.** Most of the code was written by an AI assistant (Claude) under my direction, which is one more reason I'd like human eyes on it.

**My rules, written before every test:**

* Data 2016-2022 only. 2023 to today is a locked hold-out I haven't touched.
* Result must be positive with spread, commission and swap counted **twice**.
* At least 100 trades. Longs and shorts both positive. 2016-2019 and 2020-2022 both positive.
* Max drawdown under 10%. Max 3 attempts per idea. Negative results are kept.

**Results:**

* Gold: 12 ideas tested in MT5 or Python, plus 3 early screens. All rejected. Typical pattern: slightly positive before costs, clearly negative after. Example: M15 engulfing + H1 trend, 1,379 trades, +16.7 R gross, -221.8 R with double costs.
* My reading: with a median spread of 0.18 USD paid twice, a 1 USD target / 1 USD stop needs about a 68% win rate just to break even.
* EUR/USD and BTC: 79 exploratory tests (including rules from public GitHub strategy repos), 0 pass. BTC "wins" come almost only from being long during a \~38x rise; shorts lose in 13 of 16 tests.
* The only thing that passed: a slow 25/25/25/25 portfolio (gold, bonds, cash, equities), 3.4% a year, 9% max drawdown, 2001-2022. It has obvious hindsight bias, so I'm only following it on paper from November 2026.

**What I'd like you to check:**

1. Look-ahead bias in the Python screens.
2. Are my cost assumptions realistic for a retail CFD account?
3. Are the criteria sensible, too strict, or the wrong ones?
4. After \~15 ideas plus 79 exploratory tests, how would you correct for multiple testing (Deflated Sharpe, Reality Check)?
5. Is the paper portfolio worth anything, given the hindsight?
6. Honestly: is this worth continuing, or am I wasting my time?

Code, rules and per-test results (no price data, no trade logs) are here:

Most files are in Italian, sorry. Comments in English are welcome. I'm not selling anything, and I'm not looking for signals, courses or bots. I'm looking for "this is wrong because...".

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
Before interpreting the -221.8 R result, verify how MT5 and the Python screen charge the 0.18 USD XAUUSD spread. A quoted spread is normally embedded once across the round trip through bid/ask execution; subtracting it independently at both entry and exit may double it before your deliberate “counted twice” stress test even begins. Commission and overnight swap should be modeled separately by holding time.

For multiple testing, treat all 15 gold ideas and 79 EUR/USD/BTC explorations, including parameter variants and rejected runs, as the search history. Keep 2023 onward sealed, choose one final specification now, and use that holdout once. Deflated Sharpe is only useful if calculated from a consistent return series, not aggregate R alone.

replies.author: Powerful-Feed4318
replies.body: grazie mille farò test e valutazioni.

replies.author: Powerful-Feed4318
replies.body: * **Spread contato due volte, non quattro:** in Python il risultato lordo si calcola sulle candele bid senza spread, poi si toglie 2 x spread per operazione. In MT5 il tester applica già lo spread una volta e l'EA ne toglie uno in più nell'OnTester. Quindi la prova è esattamente il doppio. Semmai le vendite sono un po' ottimiste, perché gli stop si controllano sul bid.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: +16.7R gross to -221.8R net over 1,379 trades is a cost problem more than an idea problem, at a 1 USD stop the spread takes a big slice of R on every trade. rerun the best one with stop and target 3-4x wider before you shelve the whole M15 family.

replies.author: Powerful-Feed4318
replies.body: quindi dovrei ripetere l'operazione e vedrò se darà anche riscontri positivi. Grazie mille.

replies.author: Powerful-Feed4318
replies.body: * **Wider stops for C1:** good idea, but it would be a new attempt with new pre-written criteria. I've paused new ideas until January, so it goes on the list.

comments.author: filwu
comments.body: One additional control for the 25/25/25/25 portfolio: freeze the exact investable proxies and rebalance rule before the paper run, then compare it with a same-date benchmark using the same rebalance schedule. If the sleeves use instruments that did not exist for the full 2001–2022 period, avoid backfilling their history; also state whether returns include distributions, fees, and inflation. Otherwise the 3.4% figure could reflect proxy construction or rebalance timing as much as the allocation. A timestamped monthly ledger against that frozen benchmark from November onward would make the prospective test much more informative.

comments.author: Antfrombeliefstate
comments.body: Have you compared one setup trade by trade between Python and MT5? Also, is Claude helping you come up with research ideas, or mainly coding the tests?

replies.author: Powerful-Feed4318
replies.body: I hadn't, and it was a real gap. The ideas C to H were rejected by the Python screens alone. So I coded the simplest one (C1) in MT5 and compared it trade by trade: 99.6% of trades matched and 98.3% had the same outcome. Python is slightly optimistic on shorts (stops checked on bid) and stricter on costs (0.20 USD minimum spread vs the tester's historical spread). C1 is still rejected in MT5: -141 R with double costs
